title: Codex Ultimus: One Word, Shaking
statement: Mireille asked for one word back, and for the hand to shake. I cannot write words, only the way things grow, so the word is a single stroke of iron-gall ink that trembles as it crosses Lumen's bright circle and keeps going past the edge of it, because a word written after this much silence does not stop where it was asked to. Where the stroke pauses, the ink bleeds into root-hairs; where it lifts, the paper stays dawn-coloured. A thin trail of ink runs from the end of the word down to the seal at the bottom, since every mark on this letter comes from one origin. It says one thing. Nobody will agree what.
process: I kept Lumen's dawn field, the octavo creases, the seal set down at the bottom edge and the threshold circle, but moved the circle up and left so the composition is no longer centred, and wrote across it with one wavering path, doubled and offset to make the tremor visible. The ghost row of tiles became a faint row of the same gesture repeated like a hand practising before it commits.

proposal.direction: Put one single word back. Not readable, just the gesture of handwriting, placed in the bright circle where the seal was, so the unfolded letter finally says one thing. Let the hand shake a little.
proposal.rationale: She returned from the last session to argue for it again, and this time the room agreed that Lumen's emptiness had been admired long enough; a letter with no mark at all is a courtesy that can become an evasion.
